newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: North Korea strikes barter deal with Cargill.
newsitem.headline: North Korea strikes barter deal with Cargill.

text.p: North Korea has agreed to barter about 4,000 tonnes of zinc for about 20,000 tonnes of wheat from U.S. grains giant Cargill Inc, traders in Seoul close to the deal said on Tuesday.
The deal was struck in Beijing last Saturday, the traders said. The wheat shipment was expected in leave the United States in early May and arrive in North Korea later in the month.
Traders valued the wheat shipment at about $4 million, roughly equal to the value of the zinc.

Earlier, U.S. officials said it was probably the first direct sale of U.S. grown wheat to North Korea since the end of the 1950-53 Korean War, when Washington imposed a tight ban on trade with Pyongyang.
Cargill and North Korea have been discussing the wheat sale since January following approval by the U.S. government to sell 500,000 tonnes of wheat and/or rice to the communist country.
